items.q: Which iron study pattern defines iron deficiency anaemia?
o: Low ferritin, high binding capacity, low saturation
items.exp: Iron deficiency empties stores so ferritin falls, the liver raises transferrin (binding capacity) and saturation drops. Chronic disease does the opposite for binding capacity.
r: Incorrect. Binding capacity rises in deficiency, not falls.
Correct. Low ferritin plus high binding capacity plus low saturation.
Incorrect. High saturation suggests overload or sideroblastic states.
Incorrect. Ring sideroblasts indicate sideroblastic anaemia.
items.kp: Deficiency: ferritin down, binding capacity up.

items.q: A microcytic patient has haemoglobin 10 g/dL, MCV 62 fL and red cell count 5.8 million. Mentzer index is about 10.7. What is most likely?
items.exp: Mentzer index (MCV divided by red cell count) below 13 favours thalassaemia trait, supported by a high red cell count despite anaemia. Iron studies and electrophoresis confirm it.
r: Incorrect. Iron deficiency usually gives an index above 13.
Correct. Index below 13 with high count favours thalassaemia trait.
Incorrect. Aplastic anaemia is usually normocytic or macrocytic.
Incorrect. Megaloblastic anaemia is macrocytic, not microcytic.
items.kp: Many small cells with low Mentzer index means thalassaemia trait.

items.q: During pneumonia a patient has microcytic anaemia with ferritin in the normal range. What is the correct interpretation?
o: Ferritin may be raised by inflammation, so deficiency is not excluded
items.exp: Ferritin is an acute phase reactant raised by infection and inflammation, so a normal value cannot exclude iron deficiency during illness. Very low ferritin would still prove deficiency.
r: Incorrect. Inflammation masks deficiency through ferritin.
Correct. Normal ferritin in inflammation excludes nothing.
Incorrect. Electrophoresis is needed to prove thalassaemia.
Incorrect. Overload needs high saturation evidence.
items.kp: Never trust a normal ferritin in an inflamed patient.

items.q: Koilonychia, angular cheilitis and pica are classic tissue signs of which deficiency?
items.exp: Chronic iron deficiency affects epithelial tissues producing spoon shaped nails, mouth corner sores, glossitis and pica. These signs reflect iron dependent enzyme failure beyond anaemia.
r: Incorrect. B12 deficiency causes glossitis with neurological signs.
Correct. These epithelial signs mark iron deficiency.
Incorrect. Folate deficiency lacks nail changes.
Incorrect. Vitamin C causes scurvy with gum and wound signs.
items.kp: Spoon nails plus pica points to iron deficiency.

items.q: Ring sideroblasts in marrow with high serum iron indicate which anaemia?
items.exp: Sideroblastic anaemia fails to insert iron into haem, so iron rings mitochondria in precursors while systemic iron rises. Alcohol, lead, isoniazid and inherited defects are causes.
r: Incorrect. Deficiency has empty stores and no rings.
Correct. Iron rings with high iron mean sideroblastic anaemia.
Incorrect. Thalassaemia major shows ineffective erythropoiesis without this definition.
Incorrect. Chronic disease sequesters iron without ring forms.
items.kp: Ring sideroblast means iron present but unusable for haem.

items.q: Basophilic stippling of red cells with abdominal pain and wrist drop suggests which poisoning?
items.exp: Lead impairs haem synthesis enzymes and ribonuclease, causing stippling, microcytic anaemia, colic and motor neuropathy with wrist drop. Blood lead measurement confirms exposure.
r: Incorrect. Arsenic causes gut and skin changes with Mees lines.
Correct. Stippling plus wrist drop means lead.
Incorrect. Mercury causes tremor and renal injury.
Incorrect. Copper excess causes liver and brain disease in Wilson disease.
items.kp: Stippled cells plus wrist drop: check blood lead.

items.q: An elderly man has iron deficiency anaemia without dietary explanation. What must be excluded first?
items.exp: Iron deficiency in adult men and postmenopausal women signals gastrointestinal blood loss until proven otherwise, including colorectal cancer. Endoscopic evaluation is mandatory.
r: Incorrect. Trait is lifelong and would not newly present this way.
Correct. Exclude gut blood loss and malignancy first.
Incorrect. Haemolysis causes reticulocytosis and jaundice patterns.
Incorrect. Renal anaemia is usually normocytic from erythropoietin lack.
items.kp: Older adult iron deficiency equals gut loss until proven otherwise.

items.q: Anaemia of chronic disease is driven mainly by which mediator raising hepcidin?
items.exp: Interleukin 6 stimulates hepatic hepcidin, which traps iron in macrophages and blocks gut absorption, restricting red cell production despite adequate stores.
r: Incorrect. Erythropoietin stimulates red cell production.
Correct. Interleukin 6 raises hepcidin and sequesters iron.
Incorrect. Vitamin D does not drive this anaemia.
Incorrect. Thrombopoietin regulates platelets.
items.kp: Hepcidin is the iron gatekeeper raised by inflammation.

items.q: Which finding most favours thalassaemia trait over iron deficiency?
o: Target cells with normal iron studies and raised HbA2
items.exp: Beta thalassaemia trait raises HbA2 on electrophoresis with target cells and normal iron studies. Iron deficiency widens distribution width and lowers ferritin instead.
r: Incorrect. Wide width favours iron deficiency.
Correct. Raised HbA2 with target cells means beta trait.
Incorrect. Low ferritin proves iron deficiency.
Incorrect. Trait does not correct with iron.
items.kp: Prove trait with HbA2, not by iron trial alone.

items.q: After starting iron therapy, which response confirms iron deficiency treatment effect earliest?
o: Reticulocyte rise within about a week
items.exp: Reticulocytes rise first within days to a week as marrow receives iron, followed by haemoglobin rise over weeks. Ferritin and MCV normalise later during continued therapy.
r: Incorrect. Ferritin recovers over months, not days.
Correct. Reticulocytosis is the earliest response.
Incorrect. Cell size corrects over the red cell lifespan.
Incorrect. Platelet changes do not confirm response.
items.kp: Check reticulocytes first when judging iron response.
